chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from Ismāʿīl al-Juʿfī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The woman with istiḥāḍah refrains for the days of her menstrual period, then she observes precaution for one day or two. If she sees purity, she performs ghusl, and if she does not see purity, she performs ghusl and uses cotton; then she continues to perform salat with that ghusl until blood appears on the cotton. When it appears, she repeats the ghusl and replaces the cotton.

His statement, 'she observes precaution for one day or two,' applies when her habitual period is less than ten days: she observes precaution for one day or two. But as for one whose habit is ten days, she has no right to extend precaution by anything further; rather, the ruling of the woman with istiḥāḍah becomes binding upon her according to what we have mentioned. Likewise is the meaning of everything narrated concerning her extending precaution by one day, two days, or three.
(489) 61. Similar to what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Abī Jaʿfar, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the menstruating woman: how long does she extend precaution? He said, 'She extends precaution by one day, or two days, or three.'

key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: cotton used to check or absorb blood
key_terms.اَلْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular uterine bleeding outside menstruation
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she extends precaution beyond the habitual menstrual days
key_terms.طُهْرًا: a state of purity from bleeding

ai.seo_question: How long does a menstruating woman extend precaution before being treated as a woman with istiḥāḍah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal rulings concerning a woman in istiḥāḍah and the period of precaution after the days of her habitual menstruation. It explains when ghusl is required, how long precaution may continue, and clarifies that a woman whose habitual period is ten days does not extend beyond that and instead takes the ruling of istiḥāḍah.
